purpose.description: Determine how identifiability behaves when multiple individually insufficient interfaces are composed into a joint observation system.
purpose.role: Test whether interface composition can create sufficient access through complementary information channels.
not_used_for: assuming independent interfaces are always additive
equating more sensors with guaranteed identifiability

system_class.description: Systems evaluated under multiple observation interfaces.

representative_compositions.interpretation: Different views of system dynamics jointly preserve target distinctions.
Redundant observations do not restore missing distinctions.

strict_improvement.statement: Adding an interface can improve identifiability only if it separates previously merged observation classes.

redundancy.statement: Additional interfaces may add no target-relevant information.

minimal_composition_analysis.interpretation: The minimum interface may be distributed across multiple observation channels.

failure_analysis.common_failure: shared blind spot across all composed interfaces

condition.statement: There exists f_a,f_b where all component observations agree but target differs.

theoretical_connection.new_result: Identifiability is a property of composed information geometry, not individual sensors.

decision.meaning: Interface composition can create identifiability when combined views eliminate target-relevant ambiguity.

notes: The correct unit of analysis is the information preserved by the composed interface.
More observations help only when they reduce target ambiguity.
Composition provides a bridge from fixed interfaces to adaptive sensing systems.
